## 1. Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
#| label: setup-environment

rm(list = ls()[!sapply(ls(), function(x) is.function(get(x)))])
cat("\014")
options(scipen = 999)

# Keep non-ASCII characters (>=, em-dash) intact in figures and printed output.
# Running from a bare terminal can start R in a non-UTF-8 locale, which silently
# turns them into "<U+2265>" in plot labels and console output. RStudio already
# sets a UTF-8 locale, so this is only a safety net for terminal/CI runs.
if (!isTRUE(l10n_info()[["UTF-8"]])) {
  invisible(suppressWarnings(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "en_US.UTF-8")))
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# HOW MUCH IS THIS POST *ABOUT* DIET?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Here we select posts that mention at least one diet term. 
# Yet, mentioning a diet word isn't the same as talking about diet. Someone can write three
# paragraphs about their prednisone and end with "oh, and I've cut out sugar" — that's
# a diet mention, but the post isn't about diet. We want a score that tells the two
# apart, so we can look at the posts where food really is the subject.

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(arrow)
library(tidytext)
library(knitr)

source(here("config.R"))

if (!exists("perc_table")) {
  perc_table <- function(df, column_name) {
    df |>
      count(!!rlang::sym(column_name), sort = TRUE, name = "count") |>
      mutate(
        relative_freq_pct = (count / sum(count)) * 100,
        cumulative_freq_pct = cumsum(relative_freq_pct),
        across(ends_with("_pct"), ~ round(.x, 1))
      )
  }
}
```

## 2. Load lemmatized subreddit data and word list

```{r}
#| message: false
#| label: load-data

df <- arrow::read_feather(
  file.path(DATA_PATH, "data/myo_dys_subreddits_lemmatized_2005_jul2026.feather")
)

diet_terms_lemmatized <- readRDS(
  file.path(DATA_PATH, "word_lists/diet_terms_lemmatized.RDS")
)

cat("Loaded", scales::comma(nrow(df)), "subreddit posts\n")
cat("Diet word list:", nrow(diet_terms_lemmatized), "terms\n")
print(df |> count(disease_type))
```

## 3. Tokenize and match diet terms

```{r}
#| message: false
#| label: tokenize-and-match

tokens <- df |>
  select(doc_id, text = lemmatized_text) |>
  filter(!is.na(text)) |>
  unnest_tokens(word, text)

cat("Total tokens:", scales::comma(nrow(tokens)), "\n")

all_diet_matches <- tokens |>
  inner_join(diet_terms_lemmatized, by = "word") |>
  select(doc_id, word)

cat("Total diet term matches:", scales::comma(nrow(all_diet_matches)), "\n")
cat("Posts with at least one match:", scales::comma(n_distinct(all_diet_matches$doc_id)), "\n")

diet_counts_per_post <- all_diet_matches |>
  group_by(doc_id) |>
  summarise(
    n_diet_tokens = n(),
    n_diet_terms  = n_distinct(word),
    diet_terms_matched = paste(sort(unique(word)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

if ("n_tokens" %in% names(df)) df <- df |> select(-n_tokens)
post_len <- tokens |> count(doc_id, name = "n_tokens")

df <- df |>
  left_join(post_len, by = "doc_id") |>
  left_join(diet_counts_per_post, by = "doc_id") |>
  mutate(
    n_tokens      = replace_na(n_tokens, 0L),
    n_diet_tokens = replace_na(n_diet_tokens, 0L),
    n_diet_terms  = replace_na(n_diet_terms, 0L),
    diet_terms_matched = replace_na(diet_terms_matched, "")
  )
```

## 4. Diet centrality score

```{r}
#| message: false
#| label: diet-centrality

# Diet centrality score is built from two parts:
#   1. How dense? What share of the post's words are diet words. One diet word in a
#      50-word post may be background noise; ten in a 50-word post is clearly on-topic.
#   2. How varied? How many DIFFERENT diet words appear. Saying "protein" eight times
#      is one idea repeated; saying protein, carbs, calories and fibre sounds more like 
#.     a genuine discussion of nutrition. We take a log of this so the count still counts, 
#      but going from 1 to 2 different words matters more than going from 9 to 10.
# Multiply the two together results in the diet centrality score.

df <- df |>
  mutate(
    diet_density    = n_diet_tokens / pmax(n_tokens, 1),
    diet_centrality = diet_density * log1p(n_diet_terms)
  )

# From here on we only look at posts that mention diet at all (see the note below on
# why the posts with no diet words have to be left out).
df_diet <- df |>
  filter(n_diet_tokens > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(diet_centrality))

cat("=== Diet Centrality Summary (diet posts) ===\n")
cat("Diet posts (>= 1 diet term):", scales::comma(nrow(df_diet)), "\n")
cat("Median diet centrality:", round(median(df_diet$diet_centrality), 4), "\n")
cat("Max diet centrality:", round(max(df_diet$diet_centrality), 4), "\n")

# Correcting for post length.
# The score above has a built-in bias: short posts score high too easily. A two-line
# "anyone tried creatine?" is nearly all diet words, while a long, thoughtful post
# about someone's nutrition gets diluted by everything else they wrote. Left alone,
# we'd end up studying one-liners.
#
# So we fit a line describing the usual relationship between post length and the
# score, then keep the RESIDUAL — how far each post sits above or below what's typical
# for a post of its length. A positive residual means: for its size, this post is
# unusually focused on diet. That residual is what we use from here on, and the
# printouts below confirm the length bias is gone afterwards (r drops to ~0).
#
# Posts with no diet words get no score (NA).

r_test <- cor.test(df_diet$n_tokens, df_diet$diet_centrality)
cat(sprintf("\nLength vs raw centrality (diet posts): r = %.3f, p = %.2e\n",
            r_test$estimate, r_test$p.value))

fit <- lm(diet_centrality ~ log1p(n_tokens), data = df_diet)
df_diet$diet_centrality_adj <- residuals(fit)
cat(sprintf("Model R-squared: %.3f, slope: %.5f\n", summary(fit)$r.squared, coef(fit)[2]))

r_adj <- cor.test(df_diet$n_tokens, df_diet$diet_centrality_adj)
cat(sprintf("After adjustment: r = %.3f, p = %.3f\n", r_adj$estimate, r_adj$p.value))

# Put the adjusted score back on the full dataset (posts with no diet words get NA).
df <- df |> left_join(df_diet |> select(doc_id, diet_centrality_adj), by = "doc_id")
df_diet <- df_diet |> arrange(desc(diet_centrality_adj))
```

## 5. Summary: diet-mention rate by disease group

```{r}
#| message: false
#| label: summary

cat("=== Diet-mention rate by disease group ===\n")
df |>
  summarise(
    n_posts = n(),
    n_diet_posts = sum(n_diet_tokens > 0),
    pct_diet = round(mean(n_diet_tokens > 0) * 100, 1),
    .by = disease_type
  ) |>
  print()

cat("\n=== Diet posts by subreddit ===\n")
df_diet |> count(subreddit, disease_type, sort = TRUE) |> print()

cat("\n=== Top 20 diet terms ===\n")
all_diet_matches |>
  count(word, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 20) |>
  print()

# Cutoff comparison
cutoff_table <- tibble(
  Criterion = c("any diet term", "diet_centrality_adj > 0",
                "n_diet_terms >= 2", "n_diet_terms >= 3", "n_diet_terms >= 4"),
  `Posts remaining` = c(
    nrow(df_diet),
    sum(df_diet$diet_centrality_adj > 0),
    sum(df_diet$n_diet_terms >= 2),
    sum(df_diet$n_diet_terms >= 3),
    sum(df_diet$n_diet_terms >= 4)
  )
) |>
  mutate(`% of diet posts` = round(`Posts remaining` / nrow(df_diet) * 100, 1))
kable(cutoff_table, caption = "Diet centrality cutoffs (among posts with >= 1 diet term)")
```

## 6. Save outputs

```{r}
#| message: false
#| label: save-outputs

diet_output_path <- file.path(DATA_PATH, "data/myo_dys_subreddits_diet_posts_2005_jul2026.feather")
write_feather(df_diet, diet_output_path)
cat("Saved", scales::comma(nrow(df_diet)), "diet posts to:\n ", diet_output_path, "\n\n")

full_output_path <- file.path(DATA_PATH, "data/myo_dys_subreddits_with_diet_counts_2005_jul2026.feather")
write_feather(df, full_output_path)
cat("Saved full four-subreddit set to:\n ", full_output_path,
    "(", scales::comma(nrow(df)), "rows )\n")
```
